items.q: Step ladder fever with rose spots and relative bradycardia in week two is classically what?
items.exp: Faget pulse temperature dissociation with faint truncal macules marks enteric invasion of Peyer patches; malaria spikes cyclically with rigors instead. Blood culture confirms week one.
r: Incorrect. Dengue bleeds with rash differently.
items.kp: Step ladder plus rose spots plus slow pulse: typhoid.

items.q: Ileal perforation in the third week of untreated enteric fever occurs through which structure?
o: Ulcerated Peyer patches of the terminal ileum
items.exp: Lymphoid hyperplasia necroses into longitudinal ulcers that perforate with peritonitis; surgery with antibiotics saves while bleed warns earlier. Appendix sits proximally uninvolved.

items.q: The single most sensitive diagnostic test for enteric fever even after antibiotics is what?
items.exp: Intracellular bacilli persist in marrow macrophages despite serum sterilisation; blood cultures die with first doses while Widal needs paired rises. Marrow invasiveness limits routine use.

items.q: A rising Widal O then H titre in week two of fever means what, and what is its pitfall?
o: Acute enteric fever; single titres mislead in endemic zones
items.exp: O agglutinins rise early and fade while H persists; paired fourfold rises diagnose while lone titres reflect carriage, prior infection or cross reaction. Culture remains gold.
r: Incorrect. Fever with pattern is real.

items.q: Leukopenia with eosinopenia in prolonged step ladder fever favours enteric fever over which mimics?
items.exp: Typhoid suppresses marrow relatively while pyogenic sepsis pushes neutrophilia; smears and cultures still exclude malaria and dengue. Eosinopenia reflects acute stress.
items.kp: Typhoid marrow stays quiet, not pushed.

items.q: MDR enteric fever resistant to chloramphenicol, ampicillin and cotrimoxazole is treated with what?
items.exp: Third generation cephalosporins with macrolides bypass classic plasmid resistance; fluoroquinolones fail where gyrA mutants dominate. XDR adds carbapenem debates.

items.q: Asymptomatic food handler shedding Vi positive Salmonella Typhi in stool is managed how?
o: Exclusion with prolonged ciprofloxacin and cholecystectomy if gallstones persist
items.exp: Gallbladder biofilms shelter bacilli from short courses; clearance cultures gate return to food work while surgery cures stone associated carriage. Vaccines never treat carriers.
items.kp: Typhoid carrier cooks: exclude and clear gallbladder.

items.q: Vi conjugate typhoid vaccine (Typbar TCV) improves on Vi polysaccharide chiefly how?
o: T dependent memory protecting infants under 2 years
items.exp: Conjugation recruits T help into memory with infant immunogenicity; plain Vi needs boosters without memory over age two. Ty21a stays oral with shorter cover.

items.q: Non typhoidal Salmonella gastroenteritis 12 hours after poultry with cramps is managed how?
o: Fluids alone; antibiotics prolong carriage in uncomplicated cases
items.exp: Self limited invasion clears with support while antibiotics extend shedding and select resistance; extremes of age, prostheses and sickle cell merit therapy. Stool culture confirms.

items.q: Salmonella osteomyelitis in sickle cell disease localises classically where and why?
o: Diaphysis of long bones from microinfarct seeding
items.exp: Sickled infarcts seed gut derived bacilli into dead bone; prolonged cephalosporin courses with debridement cure while staphylococcal metaphysitis differs. Vaso occlusion sets the stage.
items.kp: Sickle bone pain with Salmonella: infarct seeded.
